         2012 when I started to create prototype mixing sessions that
         became the base of my albums AENTHERA (2016), HYPERGAME (2017)
         and DESTRONNAUTH (2019). Virtually this one was the very first
         demo track that I made for the upcoming chip-metal albums,
         other tracks were just finished first. Finally it had its place
         on the 4th album called NECROLEPSY (2022). At the moment of
         releasing this SID in 2021 the album hasn't been even mixed down
         yet so the SID cover version created for Vincenzo's C64 Grand
         Tour Challenge became the first public release." (NP)

         and jumping in and out dimensions. The title is a reference to
         Gordon Freeman from Half-Life2. defMON is a dimension jumper anyway
         so it is a good fit." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Arthrobob.sid:
COMMENT: 1RT1.0 "Originally it was a test file of Hermit's 1-RasterTracker.
         Before the release time, Knut asked Vincenzo if he could make a SID
         for his return one-part demo made for DOTY2013. Vincenzo did not
         have any time so he passed the project to me. At that moment I had
         only this raw little SID in the hatch. Finally it appeared to be
         a very nice fit to Knut's awesome bob demo part that uses perfect
         synch to the music." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Awakening.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.8 "This angry tune was created for Vandalism mag #68. It is not
         a crowd pleaser so I'd be surprised if anyone left it looping
         longer than 3 minutes. It is perfect for shoot at something and
         break or kill things, though." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Bare_Knuckle.sid:
COMMENT: MS1.2 "Heavy stuff to stretch the features of Martin Piper's

         an example tune." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Behemoth.sid:
TITLE: Hail He... [from the movie Evil Dead 2]
 ARTIST: Joseph LoDuca
COMMENT: SW1.7 "An another MIDI conversion for a 2015 Halloween release
         by Hokuto Force. The original movie score is very heavily
         orchestrated so I broke the tune down to a bass guitarist, a
         guitarist and a crazy piano player to fit in 3 channels." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Berzerk_Redux_Loa:
COMMENT: MS2.1 "Tune has a long way home: initially it existed as an audio
         track for an iPhone race game called "Freeway'86". The game had a
         C64 style mode so original SID sounds were to be included. For that
         I created six or seven of SID worktunes and some short jingles. The
         game did not reach the finish line so most of tunes eat dust. For
         Martin's MS2 online compo I fed the music data of the "Coastal"
         subtune into the proggie. Checking the tune, Martin asked if he
         can use it for the loading screen of Berzerk Redux cart version.
         It is one of my fav new-old games so I was really happy to provide
         that." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Blahblah.sid:
COMMENT: FC4.0 "That was one of the short intro tunes that I gave to a guy
         called Aero to use in his stuff during the early '90s. I don't
         know if he finished anything afterwards. I could not find him in
         CSDb archives so I guess not." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Blood_and_Thunder:
TITLE: Blood and Thunder [from Leviathan]
 ARTIST: Mastodon
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "A simple straight conversion of the original metal
         song, created for Vandalism News #66. Play it for your plants
         5x a day. After a week they will bite your dog pissing on them." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Bluesbird.sid:
COMMENT: FC4.0 "During early May of 2011 a pack of worn disks were returned
         to me that included some old SIDs and other workfiles in a massively
         unorganised form. Back in time, many times I just saved workfiles
         to gamedisks spare space and I used messy filenames. I had
         a phone/note book to keep some order in the mess. 20 years later
         this book became my only memory of certain songs. According to it,
         I still have 40-50 disks lurking around somewhere. This short tune
         was hiding on one of the retrieved old disks and as archives say
         it's one of my earliest SIDs." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Booogie_8580.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "That's a guitar boogie of mine (converted from a real
         tune) that utilises irregular rhythm patterns and funky slap bass
         line. This tune was in the pack that was given for a demo group
         called "GMC" for their debut demo called "Brand New". I don't know if
         they used any of the songs later on but as I can remember they had
         some problems with the music driver." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Borxx.sid:
TITLE: Borxx Redux [from Dramatically Different]
 ARTIST: Wackor
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "Jan Harries called it "heavy metal SID" and it's the
         closest definition for my dirty style I've heard so far. Indeed,
         the song is a collection of pre-historic heavy guitar riffs of mine.
         In 2011 it was recycled by my rock band Wackor and we wrote a metal
         song about it, called 'BORXX REDUX'. That version was also included
         in 'The Sound of SceneSat Volume 3' music collection that had 89
         tracks by musicians of the demoscene all around." (NP)
         Won the Exchipo #1 music compo in 2009.
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Breaker.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.0 "As far as I can remember it was my very first short tune
         for Hermit's SIDwizard project to test basic functions. I guess this
         my only SIDwizard tune that is not a MIDI conversion." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Bricks_n_Balls.si:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "The Shadow introduced me to Zarko who was working on a C64
         game project called Bricks'n'Walls, under Avatar flag. Zarko is a
         very cool and humbe guy with an awesome work ethic so we quickly
         got along well. His game project was a tribute to wallbreaker games
         like Krakout or Arkanoid. Out of respect, we agreed on adding a couple
         of tune covers of legendary wallbreaker music to the game project. It
         includes a lot of subtunes. The ingame ones were tricky as they had to
         be 2-channel as the 3rd channel was reserved for sound FX. The audio
         engine that provided all (+SFX) was SID-Wizard 1.9 tracker by Hermit
         who also offered some very good tech assistance on the way. About
         composing, all of the songs were recorded with a MIDI keyboard,
         arranged inside Reaper DAW and exported as 3-channel MIDI. The
         SWMconvert.exe turned it into 3-channel note data for SID-Wizard where
         the sounds became added / tweaked and the data assigned to subtunes.
         Using a MIDI converter is a very fast process. This way, the whole
         project took about the same time as feeding music data to a tracker
         manually for a single tune would." (NP)

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Cadmium.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "Jan invited me to SIDwave shortly after Borxx was released.

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Cassiopeia.sid:

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Chaos_Theory.sid:
TITLE: Rude Awakening [from the PC demo Chaos Theory]

COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "A conversion of Chaos Theory tune from our PC demoscener
         mastermind friend Gargaj. We performed this song with SIDRIP
         Alliance during the last couple of active years." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Choronzon.sid:
TITLE: Choronzon [from Exit]
 ARTIST: Tangerine Dream
COMMENT: SW1.2 "I celebrated the release of SIDwizard 1.2 with this SID.
         I've been a fan of the original Tangerine song as it was used as
         a TV show in the old times called 'Panorama', I thought the first
         time I heard it that it would make a good SID. It took 20 years or
         so but here it is. It is completely 'wired' as I used a stripped
         down MIDI file and SIDwizard's own converter." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Chronomorph.sid:
COMMENT: GT2.7 "Based on a worktune for Wackor, called 'Time' but ended up

         place#2. Out of 2... :)" (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Clue.sid:
TITLE: The Clue [from Aenthera]
 ARTIST: NecroPolo
COMMENT: SW1.7 "Originally I created this SID tune for a youtube tutorial
         video explaining the MIDI converter utility of SIDwizard then I
         noticed Karmic's non-standard time signature compo so I released
         it there finally." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Colony.sid:
COMMENT: GT2.7 "Music dressing for the movie demo idea by LHS that won the
         demo compo at Forever 2011 Party. I had a relatively easy task: by

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Commodore_from_He:
COMMENT: SW1.4 "I made the original track of this MIDI conversion for a
         retro style PC racing game called Project Downforce around 2011.
         The original sounded like an old chiptune from some SNES machine
         so SID sound is not too far from its original form, just longer.
         A couple of years later Jazzcat asked a rocking SID for a dismag
         and I expanded the original tune, using Hermit's SWMconvert tool
         that he made for SIDwizard. The title refers to legendary PANTERA
         guitarist Dimebag Darrell. All the riffs and solos reflect his
         style, I guess he would make something like that if he made C64
         music. This SID was finally not released for the diskmag but
         in 2014 @ÁROK Party SID compo, placed #3." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Cracktro.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "Grass contacted me shortly after X2010 where the THSX
         music colly by SIDwave was released, including Destronaut pt1. He
         imagined a similar way powerful tune for his brand new pic for a
         new Avatar intro, called 'Cracktro'. I picked up an unfinished
         1994 worktune that I originally created for the Geister game
         project and started to expand/refine it. I did not have to start
         from the scratch so this SID was ready much sooner than others
         I released around that time." (NP)
         1994 workfile from the Geister pack as number $0D
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Crankshaft_Pulley:
COMMENT: GT2.75 "During Vincenzo's C64GTC I realised how magnificent
         centerpiece GoatTracker2 is. It sounds good and also so many
         trackers can load and read its workfiles. So, if you learn
         of how to use GoatTracker2, you can inject the data into
         SID-Wizard, NinjaTracker or SID-Factory so that way
         you can use various music driver codes. It is handy when you
         make something for a raster-hungry demo and convert the tune to
         NinjaTracker. About the title: my car visited the mechanic
         shop during the time and the guy there said things like
         crankshaft pulley, rollbar, flywheel or exhaust manifold." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Curable.sid:
TITLE: Curable [from Rendhagyás EP]
 ARTIST: RKH
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "This is neither a cover, nor a "real" SID tune: it's a
         work-in-progress arrangement demo from the first RKH EP, released in
         1995. It contains parts from the game tune pack "Geister"." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Deeper_Undergroun:
TITLE: Deeper Underground [from Synkronized]
 ARTIST: Jamiroquai
COMMENT: SW1.8 "Years passed but the time efficiency of SID-Wizard still
         amazes me. This sid cover needed roughly one afternoon from idea
         to finish. No repetitions, all parts are supposed to be different.
         Also a new solo was added (not in the original) that was actually
         played and recorded live on a keyboard just like I do on an album.
         The MIDI converter gives quite some freedom for instrumentalists I
         guess. Programming manually melody content of this depth would be
         quite a mindfuck. For me it took days before SID-Wizard. In some
         cases, a week perhaps." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Deepstalker.sid:
COMMENT: SDI "Sid Duzz'it is a magnificient tracker. I always wanted to
         test it and it is much better than I thought. The only downside is
         the tune export where I should use an assembler. Well I can't
         code. So most probably this tune will be a single-shot tune
         for the actual round of C64 Grand Tour Challenge using SDI. It
         was fun to do as it was created with a guitar in my hands so it
         is metal and was inspired by movie: Stalker." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Demultiplexer.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "A second-gen GMC track of mine with advanced filters.
         The original file had some bugs that were fixed by iAN CooG." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Depression.sid:
COMMENT: FC4.0 "One of my very first original tunes. This dirty experimental
         song defined all my following ones in a way or an another. Certain
         parts were used in the first Wackor album opening song, "Khemotox
         BloodPaint", released in 2004 by Holosonic Music." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Destronaut_1.sid:
COMMENT: GT2.7 "This 2-part piece is among the first ones I composed with
         GoatTracker 2, playing 2x speed. The tunes include lots of real guitar
         riffs. Both parts were included in the THSX music collection." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Destronaut_2.sid:
COMMENT: GT2.7 "This 2-part piece is among the first ones I composed with
         GoatTracker 2, playing 2x speed. The tunes include lots of real guitar
         riffs. Its "home" SIDwave demo delayed for months so I detached this
         part and released it in Euskal. Later, both parts were included in the
         THSX music collection." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Dirk_Gently.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "I think I don't have to introduce Dirk Gently's
         Holistic Detective Agency by the amazing Douglas Adams. But as it
         happened, it was his other work The Hitchhiker's Guide to the
         Galaxy that I read around the time. I had to wait a lot during a
         series of medical examinations and I thought it is a good excuse
         to re-read the trilogy of five, with all the spinoffs. So instead
         of the actual title, it is rather a sort of tribute to the great
         Douglas Adams, my most fav writer. About the usual tech side,
         as a SID-Wizard Emulator tune, apart from setting the sounds
         in the tracker, 99% of the work was done with a MIDI keyboard
         such as composing, orchestrating and performing / recording.
         Of course I used Hermit's smart MIDI converter tool
         SWMconver.exe as always." (NP)
         Won first place at the Arok 2024 music competition.
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Dreambreaker.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "Dreamcatcher, Dreambreaker and X-Istence belong
         together. They tell a story in this sequence. The exact inversion
         of their release dates actually. It was my compo tune for 2023
         ÁROK Party, landing #2." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Dreamcatcher.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "Dreamcatcher, Dreambreaker and X-Istence belong
         together. They tell a story in this sequence. The exact inversion
         of their release dates actually. This one was included in diskmag
         Overshadow number 40." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Eucalyptus.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "Title tune for a "save the little cute koala" game from the
         early '90s. Never released. Developer was a female C64 graphician
         called Paula or something. All I can remember is she was a hot
         redhead and boobs were epic." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Everything_Counts:
TITLE: Everything Counts [from Construction Time Again]
 ARTIST: Depeche Mode
COMMENT: FC4.0 "That was one of the short intro tunes that I gave to a guy
         called Aero to use in his stuff during the early '90s. I don't
         know if he finished anything afterwards. I could not find him in
         CSDb archives so I guess not." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Excess_Intro.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.8 "My friend AGod invited me to create music for this 30th
         anniversary Excess demo. It was fun to do. Excess kicks major
         ass! I have massive respect for the group. The tune itself is
         of course SID-Wizard and MIDI conversion. Around the time of
         creation (spring 2021) I believed that it will be released in
         weeks so I shot a video of the tracker, timed it on Youtube
         and forgot about it. As it turned out the demo itself became
         released much later (November-something?) so the audio became
         accidentally leaked on Youtube around May. Oooops..." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Experiment_Zeta.s:
COMMENT: Virtuoso 1.02 "Despite that Virtuoso is a very nice tool, it is
         not my tool. You have to keep a rather big number of cross
         references of various tables in mind compared to other tackers
         that means an ample of tiny calculations. Well, I am really bad
         at calculations. I always make mistakes. So composing was like
         20% of composing and 80% of fixing my bad calculations. As a
         consequence the tune for this C64GTC round became very short and
         simple." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Fender_of_the_Cro:
TITLE: The Raid [from the Amiga game Defender of the Crown] (0:00)
 ARTIST: Jim Cuomo
  TITLE: The Saxon Maid [from the Amiga game Defender of the Crown] (1:47)
 ARTIST: Jim Cuomo
COMMENT: NT2.03 "Shortly after my SID remix album 'rakBIT' was released
         including a remix of Richard's brilliant 'Rimrunner', Jazzcat
         contacted me and asked to join the Richard Joseph (R.I.P.)
         tribute demo project with a C64 remake of one of Richard's great
         SIDs, a tune of my choice. It's been an honour to be invited: I
         respect Richard and admire his works much, not to mention the fine
         array of SID composers who also contributed to the demo. This remake
         was made in a rather short time and it includes very old ideas of
         mine that are rooted back in '89. The SID was named after the guitar
         that I used to grab the notes." (NP)
         Covers /MUSICIANS/J/Joseph_Richard/Defender_of_the_Crown.sid,

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/GMC-Brandnew.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "That was my first complete track composed with Game Music

         my early SID composer days. This tune was in the pack that was given
         for a demo group called "GMC" for their debut called "Brand New".

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/GP_Cars.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 + SW1.9-EMU "This game music pack has approximately a
         decade-old history. When we started to create stuff with LHS
         he mentioned that he has a race game project that was already 10
         years old even by then. The very first music track I created for
         the game was a special edition of my engine FX tune Cadmium,
         around 2010. Then years passed, SID-Wizard and MIDI conversion
         came out. Many tiny tunes became added and detached from the
         project, like yellowstorm.sid that was intended to be used in
         GP Cars initially. Then the game started to get its final form
         in 2022, so did the music. The in-game tunes were created with
         the super-flexible SW-EMU. I must emphasize that the amazing
         3...2...1... FX and most others are not mine. They were

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Geister.sid:
COMMENT: GMC1.6 "My second (and last) game tune back in the time, created for

TITLE: Végtelen vidék [from album Sárkányfejezet]
 ARTIST: Diabolus in Musica
COMMENT: SW1.8 "That is where 20 minutes can bring you with SID-Wizard.
         I wanted to do something for the final round of C64 Grand Tour
         challenge that no other tracker can do so I recorded a short
         tune with an Arturia Keylab49 keyboard in Reaper, quantised
         and arranged channels for a better conversion, exported a
         3-channel MIDI file, ran swmconvert.exe on it and set the
         sounds and some other stuff. The music data is not touched so
         virtually it is me playing the keyboard. SID-Wizard is a
         beast of workflow. The title refers to Yennefer from Witcher
         books, also my childhood as our garden was full of lilac and
         gooseberries. By today, due to climate change they all gone
         around my area so that fragrance and memories of the taste
         also remind me of good people who gone and it completely rips
         my heart out. After those flashbacks I can't find my way for
         days. Anyway, this tune is included on Diabouls in Musica LP
         with lyrics and acoustic guitars. Coupled with deep lyrics
         I always have to focus to the extreme to not to collapse mentally
         during live shows when we perform this song called 'Végtelen
         vidék' or 'Infinite Landscape' as it is about letting it go and
         saying goodbye forever inevitably." (NP)

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Thanx_iAN.sid:
COMMENT: MS2 "Dedicated to iAN CooG. Bass theme is borrowed from a '90s
         Teleclub TV tune, the solo is original. It was a FC4.0 tune frag
         from '91 that many years later (2009) I sent to iAN saying thanks
         for all the help. He suggested expanding it a little so here it is.
         This vesion is fully re-worked with Martin Piper's multiplatform
         editor and was included as an example tune" (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Time_Paradox_Ninf:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "We had an idea to connect our previous Level 64 demo
         'Ninfa' from 2012 with the new one 'Time Paradox' from 2026 so they
         end with the same bit of music. The plan was to use Hermit's infinite
         wave FX in SID-Wizard that was used in Ninfa but unfortunately the SW
         player was too raster hungry for the last part of Time Paradox so we
         made an eco-class NinjaTracker2 version of it for the demo. But this
         was the original one, using the same sound as Ninfa." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Time_Paradox_tune:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "To create this demo we used a video sequencer and
         bits'n'pieces from my music score for TV drama 'Henry IV' by
         Pirandello. Finally it never became released so Time Paradox is the
         first appearance. This demo is very special to me because we met Level
         64 guys the very first time on X party '26 where it was released,
         after all those years of working together. As for the tech side it is
         a SW tune of mine so it is a MIDI conversion. We used a video
         sequencer to sync it all together so basically it is me playing the
         keyboard while watching the screen action, the very same method that I
         use for film score composing." (NP)

COMMENT: Reduced version of /MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Time_Paradox_Ninfa_remix.sid,

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Trabant_601.sid:
COMMENT: Sosperec "Many old editors are like shitbox cars like Trabant 601 from
         East Germany. The Trabant wasn't good in anything, well, apart from,
         falling apart quickly. It is unfair to say Sosperec is an utter
         shitbox as it has some clever ideas but it freezes like hell and there
         was no documentation so... Baaaaaaaah I will never touch that again.
         Definitely it was the hardest nut to crack during C64 Grand Tour
         Challenge.
         The result is this super-uninspired tune that consists of the
         first 3 instruments that did not freeze the tracker." (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Trans_Nomad_Expre:
TITLE: Trans Nomad Express [from Back to Folk (Music from Folkland)]
 ARTIST: Kerekes Band
COMMENT: SW1.7 "My friend Vincenzo asked me to tweak'n'trim the sounds
         of this tune for his coming Kerekes Band tribute music colly." (NP)
TITLE: Honolulu (from album Highway $FFFF)
 ARTIST: NecroPolo
COMMENT: MS2 "Basically it is an extended version of my tune called 'Thanx iAN'
         from 2010. It was a FC4.0 tune frag from '91 and was finished two
         decades later to iAN CooG's suggestion. It became released with Music
         Studio 2 as an example tune.
         Then it was ported to my friend Karl Burnett's retro game project
         called Freeway'86 that did not reach the finish line. Still, years
         later an album was created out of all the Nintendo64-stlye tracks.
         This one was called Honolulu. A decade later the
         original 'Thanx iAN' C64 tune was chosen by Martin Piper for his
         playable parallax scroll tech demo Tusari 2. I told him like, 'hey what
         about including an extended version that once belonged to an unreleased
         game?'. He agreed and that's how this tune came to be in 2025." (NP)
         See also /MUSICIANS/N/NECROPOLO/Thanx_iAN.sid
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Wavemode.sid:
COMMENT: NT2.04 "This tune was created for the 2025 Lethargy demo under the
         same title. It is a straight GoatTracker 2.75 -> NinjaTracker 2.04
         conversion as coder guys asked for a very slim music driver and the
         barebone NT2 is great there. For a good compatibility very simple
         instruments, structure and sounds were used so the NT2 version sounds
         almost 100% identical to the GT2 version where the tune was assembled
         in its advanced editing interface." (NP)
TITLE: We Will Rock You [from News of the World]
 ARTIST: Queen
COMMENT: FC4.0 "The first complete SID tune I ever created on C64. It was my
         very first SID tune ever and my very first steps with Future Composer

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/World_Is_Mine.sid:

/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/Worlds_Apart.sid:
TITLE: Ecce Homo [from Sárkányfejezet]
 ARTIST: Diabolus in Musica
COMMENT: GT2.7 "This is an older worktune that I composed on guitar around
         2000 or so. It did not fit any of my bands so it rested in the box.
         My 'entry composition' for Avatar was a game tunes and FX pack. The
         ingame tune needed to be slow-flow and relaxed so I dusted off this
         one. Some time later I re-created it with Goat Tracker2 and expanded
         it to 3-channels (the gametune is 2-channels) and added a second
         part including heavy riffs. It wanted to release it at
         Revision 2012 but I missed the deadline as we arrived right after
         the oldschool music compo. So, it became released a little later at
         Flashback 2012. Then, a massive leap to 2022 where I showed music
         pieces for the members of my off-scene project Diabolus in musica.
         Finally, this tune ended up to be a supermassive final track for
         the band's 2023 album "Sárkányfejezet", titled 'Ecce Homo'. (NP)
/MUSICIANS/N/NecroPolo/X-Istence.sid:
COMMENT: SW1.9-EMU "Dreamcatcher, Dreambreaker and X-Istence belong
         together. They tell a story in this sequence: Dreamcatcher,
         Dreambreaker, X-Istence. The exact inversion of their release
         dates actually. X-Istence was my tune for X2023. It was the
         first tune on the compo where the PA system fucked it up
         during the first 2 minutes or so. I guess listeners thought
         it sounds fucked up intentionally. Well it wasn't. I'm honestly
         surprised that it did not end up last on the compo :D" (NP)
